scenarios.title: The last quarter becomes the whole year
scenarios.prompt: An employee had one difficult final quarter. The annual review now focuses almost entirely on that period and gives little weight to earlier results.
scenarios.question: What is the best first correction?

options.text: Use the same predefined criteria across the full review period and inspect evidence by period.
Trust the manager’s memory because recent work is usually the most relevant.
Ask the employee to provide only their three strongest examples.

scenarios.explanation: Recent events are easier to recall. Predefined criteria and period coverage reduce the chance that one vivid interval becomes the entire evaluation.
missingEvidence: Evidence across the full review period.
Criteria and expectations set before the review.
Comparable treatment of positive and negative examples.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Availability may explain the heavy focus on recent events. The latest quarter can still deserve more weight when the role or expectations changed.
scenarios.nextAction: Build a criterion-by-period evidence table before setting the rating.

scenarios.title: A good result proves a good process
scenarios.prompt: A manager skipped required checks but the project succeeded. The review treats the success as proof that the manager’s approach was excellent.
scenarios.question: What should be evaluated separately?

options.text: The quality of the decision process using what was known before the outcome.
Only the final business result because process is secondary.
Whether the manager can tell a convincing success story.

scenarios.explanation: Good outcomes can follow weak processes. A decision record helps judge whether the risk was understood and managed before luck was known.
missingEvidence: Required checks and why they existed.
Whether similar choices would perform reliably across repeated cases.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Outcome bias is a relevant lens, but process rules may also need review if they add cost without reducing meaningful risk.
scenarios.nextAction: Rate process quality and outcome quality in separate fields.
